title: I’m building a 3ds Max tool that brings video mocap and AI-generated motion into Biped workflows
author: Practical-Drama-5640
selftext:
Hi everyone! I’m developing a MaxScript/Python tool for creating and retargeting animation inside 3ds Max.  
It integrates existing models, including GVHMR, Kimodo, and optional PhysPT post-processing. I’m building the workflow and retargeting tools, not training a new AI model.  
The main features are:  
**Video mocap:** Full-body capture, supplementary finger tracking, and separate motion exports for multiple people.  
**Text-to-motion:** Generate animation from prompts through a dedicated Max UI, with seed controls.  
**Pose-to-pose:** Use poses keyed on a Biped as constraints to generate motion between them, including multiple poses within a frame range.  
**Character-specific retargeting:** Build a reference mocap rig from the Biped Figure pose to account for different body proportions, limb lengths, and spine configurations.  
**Motion cleanup:** Adjustable COM and foot-contact corrections, jitter reduction, and optional physics-based post-processing.  
**JSON save/load:** Reuse captured or generated motion without running the entire process again.  
My goal is to make these models useful in an editable Biped animation workflow, rather than just producing a motion preview.  
It’s still a work in progress. Retargeting and baking are being tested across different rigs, and finger tracking quality depends heavily on visibility and video resolution.  
For anyone using AI motion in game development: what would make this workflow useful to you? Better foot contact, more reliable retargeting, pose control, or something else?
